'''Gonzalo García Torres''' (born 24 March 2004) is a Spanish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for {{English football updater|Fulham}} club [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] and the [[Spain national football team|Spain national team]].

García joined the [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] academy as a youth player, briefly spending time with [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] before returning to Madrid. He progressed through the club's youth system and played for [[Real Madrid Castilla]], where he became one of the team's leading goalscorers. García made his first-team debut for Real Madrid and later established himself in the senior squad, notably finishing as the top scorer at the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup]]. During his time with the first team, he won [[La Liga]] before joining Fulham in 2026.

García represented [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain at under-21 level]], becoming a regular goalscorer for the side during qualification for the [[2027 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]]. He made his senior debut for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] in March 2026, appearing as a substitute in a friendly against Iraq.

==Club career==
===Early career===
García is a youth product of SEK, Club Santa Bárbara, and Jarama Race, before joining the youth academy of [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2014.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cortegana |first=Mario |date=30 June 2025 |title=The rise of Gonzalo Garcia, Real Madrid’s breakthrough star of the Club World Cup |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6458679/2025/06/29/gonzalo-garcia-real-madrid-club-world-cup/ |access-date=5 July 2025 |work=The Athletic |language=en-US |issn=}}</ref> He had a year-long stint with [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]]'s academy in 2018–19 when his family moved there, before returning to Real Madrid. In January 2022, he was promoted to [[Real Madrid Castilla]], and he made his first appearance with them in March 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.adnblanco.com/siguen-las-promociones-el-juvenil-a-gonzalo-garcia-da-el-salto-definitivo/|title=Siguen las promociones el Juvenil A: Gonzalo García da el salto definitivo|date=15 January 2022}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/primera/el-9-esta-en-la-fabrica-n/|title=El ‘9′ está en La Fábrica|first=Carlos|last=Forjanes|date=19 May 2023|website=Diario AS}}</ref> He was a prolific scorer in the [[División de Honor Juvenil de Fútbol]] in 2022–23 where he was top scorer and won the domestic U19 treble, which earned him a permanent promotion to the Castilla side.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/37691093/real-madrid-u19s-win-copa-del-campeones-complete-domestic-treble|title=Real Madrid's U19s complete domestic treble|date=20 May 2023|website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://en.as.com/soccer/real-madrid-already-have-a-new-9-in-la-fabrica-n/|title=Real Madrid already have a new ‘9′ in La Fábrica|first=Carlos|last=Forjanes|date=19 May 2023|website=Diario AS|access-date=1 September 2023|archive-date=1 September 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230901191050/https://en.as.com/soccer/real-madrid-already-have-a-new-9-in-la-fabrica-n/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
On 29 August 2023, García received his first call-up to the senior side after the starting winger [[Vinícius Júnior]] suffered an injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.managingmadrid.com/2023/8/29/23850311/gonzalo-garcia-could-feature-against-getafe|title=Gonzalo García could feature against Getafe|first=Managing|last=Madrid|date=29 August 2023|website=Managing Madrid}}</ref> He was named to the squad list for Real Madrid for the first time for a [[La Liga]] match against [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] on 2 September 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/real-madrid/2023/09/01/64f1d527ca47416d6d8b4591.html|title=Gonzalo, la novedad en la lista del Real Madrid ante el Getafe|date=1 September 2023|website=MARCA}}</ref>

On 5 February 2025, García scored his first goal for ''Los Blancos'' in stoppage time in a 3–2 away victory over [[CD Leganés|Leganés]] in the [[2024–25 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rfi.fr/en/sports/20250205-real-madrid-snatch-late-leganes-win-to-reach-copa-del-rey-semis |title=Real Madrid snatch late Leganes win to reach Copa del Rey semis |publisher=RFI |date=5 February 2025 }}</ref> He finished [[2024–25 Primera Federación|the league season]] with Castilla as top scorer with 25 goals, including a [[hat-trick]] win 5–0 against [[CF Intercity|Intercity]] and four goals in both the win 6–0 against [[Mérida AD|Mérida]] and 4–1 away victory against [[Algeciras CF|Algeciras]]. By scoring 25 goals during the 2024–25 season, Gonzalo García equaled the all-time record for most goals in a single campaign for Real Madrid Castilla—a mark previously set by [[Mariano Díaz]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=TAMARAL |first=SILVIA |date=5 May 2025 |title=Gonzalo, un récord y a Primera |url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/real-madrid/2025/05/05/gonzalo-record-primera.html |access-date=5 July 2025 |website=MARCA |language=es |archive-date=6 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250506031021/https://www.marca.com/futbol/real-madrid/2025/05/05/gonzalo-record-primera.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Gonzalo secures Primera Federación golden boot |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/academy/latest-news/gonzalo-pichichi-de-la-primera-federacion-27-05-2025 |access-date=27 June 2025 |website=www.realmadrid.com}}</ref> 

On 18 June 2025, García scored in a 1–1 draw against [[Al Hilal SFC|Al-Hilal]] in the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup Group H|group stage]] match at the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]], which was also the club's first goal under new manager [[Xabi Alonso]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 June 2025 |title=Real Madrid 1–1 Al Hilal: Player Ratings As Xabi Alonso's Debut Ends in Disappointment |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/real-madrid-1-1-al-hilal-player-ratings-6-18-25 |access-date=5 July 2025 |website=SI |language=en-US}}</ref> He went on to score in a 3–0 victory against [[FC Red Bull Salzburg|Red Bull Salzburg]], helping his team advance to the knockout stage.<ref>{{cite web |last=Jackson |first=Bobbie |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cpd1n7lywgnt |title=Red Bull Salzburg 0–3 Real Madrid |publisher=BBC Sport |date=27 June 2025 }}</ref> Later, he netted the decisive goal in a 1–0 win over [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in the round of 16.<ref>{{cite web |last=Lowe |first=Sid |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/jul/01/real-madrid-juventus-club-world-cup-last-16-match-report |title=Gonzalo García downs Juventus to send Real Madrid to Club World Cup quarters |publisher=The Guardian |date=1 July 2025 }}</ref> García was awarded the top goal scorer of the Club World Cup despite Real Madrid's elimination in the semi-finals, having recorded four goals and one assist in six matches.<ref name="auto">{{cite web |title=García claims Top Goal Scorer honour |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/club-world-cup/usa-2025/articles/top-goal-scorer-race |website=[[FIFA]] |access-date=14 July 2025|date=14 July 2024}}</ref> He was later given a contract renewal until 2030 and promoted to the first team on 8 August 2025.<ref>{{cite web |title=Official announcement: Gonzalo |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-gonzalo-08-08-2025 |website=[[Real Madrid]] |access-date=8 August 2025|date=8 August 2025}}</ref> On 4 January 2026, he netted his first La Liga goals by scoring a hat-trick in a 5–1 win over [[Real Betis]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=REAL MADRID C.F. - ERROR |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/reports/cronica-real-madrid-betis-j18-liga-04-01-2026 |access-date=4 February 2026 |website=www.realmadrid.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Menzies |first=John |url=https://www.football-espana.net/2026/01/04/real-madrid-real-betis-la-liga-report |title=Gonzalo Garcia inspires Real Madrid to thumping victory in first match of 2026 |publisher=Football Espana |date=4 January 2026 }}</ref>

===Fulham===
On 3 August 2026, García signed for [[Premier League]] club [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] on a five-year contract with the ''Cottagers'' paying a fixed fee of €40 million (£34.3 million) plus an additional €2 million in performance-related add-ons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fulham sign Gonzalo|url=https://www.fulhamfc.com/news/2026/august/03/fulham-sign-gonzalo/|publisher=[[Fulham F.C.]]|date=3 August 2026|access-date=3 August 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=3 August 2026 |title=Fulham sign Gonzalo García from Real Madrid |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49523499/fulham-sign-gonzalo-garcia-real-madrid |access-date=2026-08-04 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> Real Madrid would retain an 30% sell-on-clause for any future transfer alongside matching rights, as well as a buy-back clause that would become active from García's second season onwards.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2026-08-04 |title=When Real Madrid will have the option to re-sign Gonzalo García & César Palacios |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/real-madrid-option-sign-gonzalo-210000536.html |access-date=2026-09-16 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> The move reunited García with [[Álvaro Arbeloa]], who had previously coached him at Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/arbeloa-reveals-why-wasn-t-204827470.html |title=Arbeloa reveals why it wasn’t easy to sign Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios |publisher=Yahoo! Sports |date=31 August 2026 }}</ref> Three weeks later, on 24 August, he scored his first goal on his debut in a 2–3 loss against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=read |first=Tom Masters·4 min |date=2026-08-25 |title=Five things we learned from Fulham’s 3-2 defeat to Chelsea |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/five-things-learned-fulham-3-122208355.html |access-date=2026-08-30 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Premier League recap: Chelsea beat Fulham in five-goal thriller |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49662528/premier-league-live-updates-chelsea-kick-their-season-fulham |access-date=2026-08-30 |website=www.espn.com}}</ref>

==International career==
García was a youth international for Spain, having played for the [[Spain national under-19 football team|Spain U19]]s at the [[2023 UEFA European Under-19 Championship]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/seleccion/a-por-el-12-europeo-sub-19-n/|title=¡A por el 12º Europeo Sub-19!|lang=es|first=Ignacio|last=Camacho|date=4 July 2023|website=[[Diario AS]]}}</ref>

In August 2025, he received his first call-up to the [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain U21]] for the [[2027 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification]] matches against [[Cyprus national under-21 football team|Cyprus]] and [[Kosovo national under-21 football team|Kosovo]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Gonzalo, en la primera lista de David Gordo|url=https://as.com/futbol/seleccion/gonzalo-en-la-primera-lista-de-david-gordo-n/ |lang=es |first=Ignacio |last=Camacho |website=[[MARCA]]|date=29 August 2025}}</ref> starting in both games.<ref>{{cite web |title=UEFA U21 Championship Qualification Group Stage-Group A: Spain 3-0 Cyprus |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c1w8r54v9lzt#Line-ups|website=[[BBC Sport]]|date=5 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=1-3: Gonzalo, titular en la victoria de España sub-21 ante Kosovo|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/es-ES/noticias/futbol/primer-equipo/actualidad/1-3-gonzalo-titular-en-la-victoria-de-espana-sub-21-ante-kosovo-09-09-2025 |lang=es |website=[[Real Madrid CF]] |date=9 September 2025}}</ref>

García received his first senior call-up to the [[Spain national football team|Spain]] in June 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2026-06-04 |title=Real Madrid youngster in Spain squad list for friendly vs Iraq |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/real-madrid-youngster-spain-squad-102500007.html |access-date=2026-06-17 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He made his debut on 4 June 2026, coming on in a friendly match against [[Iraq national football team|Iraq]] that ended in a 1–1 draw at the [[Estadio de Riazor]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Spain 1–1 Iraq |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/second-string-spain-held-by-iraq-low-key-world-cup-send-off-2026-06-04/ |work=Reuters |date=4 June 2026 |access-date=5 June 2026}}</ref>

==Style of play==
García is a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] capable of playing across the front line, including as a [[Winger (soccer)|winger]] on either flank, a centre-forward, or a [[second striker]]. He contributes in open play and in transitional phases. He uses his physical attributes to create space and shield the ball. During the season in which his U19 team won the domestic treble, he was involved in 25% of the team’s goals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://madriduniversal.com/19-year-old-castilla-forward-likely-to-be-called-up-for-real-madrid-vs-getafe-game/|title=19-year-old Castilla forward likely to be called up for Real Madrid vs Getafe game|first=Ash|last=Reyna|date=29 August 2023}}</ref>

García has been compared to former Real Madrid forward [[Raúl González]] due to similarities in their playing style and shared background as [[La Fábrica (Real Madrid)|La Fábrica]] graduates. The comparison gained further attention as Raúl coached García during his time at [[Real Madrid Castilla]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2 July 2025 |title=Gonzalo García: “Que me comparen con Raúl es un halago” |url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/real-madrid/2025/07/02/gonzalo-me-comparen-raul-halago.html |website=Marca |language=es |access-date=2 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date= |title=¿Quién es Gonzalo García, la nueva estrella que ilusiona al madridismo? |url=https://www.elobservador.com.uy/espana/relax/quien-es-gonzalo-garcia-la-nuestra-estrella-que-ilusiona-al-madridismo-n6006724 |website=El Observador |language=es |access-date=2 July 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
García is the second-grandnephew of Spanish-American actress [[Rita Hayworth]], the great-grandnephew of dancers [[Eduardo Cansino]] and [[Elisa Cansino]], and the great-great-grandson of dancer [[Antonio Cansino]].<ref>{{cite web|access-date=6 July 2025 |date=2 July 2025 |language=es |title=Gonzalo García: la conexión del delantero revelación del Real Madrid con Rita Hayworth |url=https://www.elmundo.es/loc/famosos/2025/07/02/686509fce85ece59148b4598.html |website=ELMUNDO}}<!-- auto-translated from Spanish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>
